outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
outline.description: Sets the stage for why RL is essential for scaling language models, outlines the challenges with existing methods, and introduces the motivation for a new algorithm.
subtopics: RL as a paradigm for language model scaling
Successes of large‑scale RL (e.g., mathematical and coding abilities)
Stability issues in current RL algorithms (GRPO, PPO)
High‑variance gradients and catastrophic model collapse
Overview of the paper’s contributions: GSPO

outline.chapter_title: Foundations: Policies, Rewards, and Importance Sampling
outline.description: Defines the mathematical notation used throughout the book and reviews the theory of importance sampling that underpins policy‑gradient methods.
subtopics: Autoregressive language models as stochastic policies
Sequence likelihood and token‑level factorization
Reward functions and normalization
Expectation under target and behavior distributions
Derivation of the importance‑sampling estimator

outline.chapter_title: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Its Limitations
outline.description: Provides a detailed exposition of PPO, its reliance on value functions, and why this becomes problematic for large language models.
subtopics: PPO objective and clipping mechanism
Token‑level importance ratios and advantage estimation
The role of the value model and its scaling challenges
Empirical issues: variance, memory, and stability

outline.description: Explains GRPO as a value‑free alternative to PPO, its formulation, and the root cause of its instability when applied to long sequences and MoE models.
subtopics: Group‑wise generation and relative advantage computation
GRPO objective and token‑level importance weights
Why GRPO removes the value model but introduces new variance
Illustrative example of gradient explosion in long responses

outline.description: Analyzes why the unit of optimization should match the unit of reward, highlighting the misalignment in GRPO and motivating a shift to sequence‑level importance ratios.
subtopics: Off‑policy learning and minibatch partitioning
Ill‑posedness of token‑level importance sampling
Variance accumulation over token steps
The principle: reward unit ↔ optimization unit

outline.description: Introduces the GSPO algorithm, its theoretical grounding, and practical implementation details.
subtopics: Sequence‑level importance ratio definition
Length‑normalization and its effect on variance
GSPO objective with group‑wise advantage
Clipping at the response level vs. token level
Pseudo‑code and integration into existing RL pipelines

outline.chapter_title: Gradient Derivation and Comparison: GSPO vs. GRPO
outline.description: Derives the gradients of GSPO and GRPO, showing how GSPO eliminates per‑token weight disparity and reduces noise.
subtopics: Derivation of the GSPO gradient (with and without clipping)
Comparison to the GRPO gradient formulation
Interpretation of equal token weighting within a sequence
Impact on stability and convergence

outline.description: Presents the token‑level variant of GSPO, its formulation, and when it is advantageous to use.
subtopics: Motivation for token‑wise advantage in multi‑turn settings
Definition of s_{i,t}(θ) with gradient stop (sg)
Objective and gradient of GSPO‑Token
Equivalence to GSPO under uniform advantage
Practical tips for choosing between GSPO and GSPO‑Token

outline.description: Details the empirical setup, benchmarks, and results that demonstrate GSPO’s superiority over GRPO.
subtopics: Model and data configuration (Qwen3‑30B‑A3B‑Base)
Training protocol: rollout batch, mini‑batching, clipping values
Performance metrics: reward curves, AIME, LiveCodeBench, CodeForces
Stability observations and training efficiency analysis
Ablation studies on clipping fractions

outline.description: Explains why MoE models are especially fragile under GRPO, the prior Routing Replay workaround, and how GSPO resolves the issue intrinsically.
subtopics: Expert‑activation volatility and its effect on token‑level ratios
Routing Replay: mechanism, overhead, and limitations
GSPO’s insensitivity to per‑token likelihood fluctuations
Empirical comparison: GRPO + Routing Replay vs. GSPO

outline.description: Discusses how GSPO simplifies system design, reduces precision constraints, and enables inference‑engine likelihood reuse.
subtopics: Precision mismatch between training and inference engines
Using inference‑engine likelihoods directly in GSPO
Benefits for partial rollouts and multi‑turn RL
Memory and communication savings

outline.description: Summarizes the key takeaways, the impact of GSPO on large‑scale RL, and potential avenues for further research.
subtopics: Recap of GSPO’s theoretical and empirical advantages
Implications for scaling RL with ever larger LMs
Open questions: adaptive clipping, curriculum of queries, hybrid token‑/sequence‑level methods
Vision for next‑generation RL‑trained language models
